methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
TAE Technologies, a Series G climate and energy company founded by Norman Rostoker and Michl Binderbauer, has raised $1.3B+ to date. The valuation universe comprises nine same-sector peers, including one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a robust peer-median approach; only one adjacent-stage peer and zero same-stage datapoints met inclusion criteria, falling short of the three-company minimum required for statistical reliability.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using $1.3B in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier for progression beyond Series G, this method implies a valuation of $1.6B. This single-method result anchors the analysis.

The valuation range supported by the analysis is $1.4B to $1.9B, with a median point of $1.6B. This narrow band reflects the absence of sufficient peer comps to triangulate multiple methods; the range is derived from the stage-progression result plus reasonable error margins. Key uncertainties include the lack of comparable financing data at TAE's exact stage and funding tier, the absence of disclosed revenue or burn metrics, and reliance on historical stage-progression multiples in a volatile frontier-tech market. A peer-median method will become viable as additional same-stage private raises surface.
